vulnerabilities.description: Weak ID generation fallback. The `idFactory` uses `Math.random()` instead of cryptographically secure random when `crypto.randomUUID()` is unavailable. This produces predictable session IDs in older environments.

Token injection via global window object. `__IMPECCABLE_TOKEN__` and `__IMPECCABLE_PORT__` are read from window globals without verification of source. If a third-party script runs before this one, it could replace these values or read them.

CSS ID escaping may be incomplete. The fallback regex in `cssId()` attempts to escape all special characters, but CSS parsing is complex and edge cases (e.g., null bytes, high Unicode) could bypass validation.

Opaque API handler references. API endpoints use hashed function references (`b('hash')`). Without seeing implementations, cannot verify these properly validate input, implement authorization, or sanitize output.

Sensitive session data in localStorage. Session state including checkpoint revisions and IDs persisted to localStorage. If the app ever handles sensitive user data in session, this is a risk under XSS attacks.

recommendations: Replace `Math.random()` fallback with `crypto.getRandomValues()` for secure ID generation (line 12, live-browser-session.js)
Wrap token injection in a `Object.freeze()` and read from a closure variable instead of window object to prevent tampering
Add `Secure` and `HttpOnly` flags to any cookies storing session tokens (verify in server config, not visible here)
Implement Content Security Policy (CSP) with `script-src 'self'` to prevent third-party script injection that could steal tokens
Verify API handlers in compiled assets implement: (1) input validation, (2) authorization checks, (3) output sanitization
For any sensitive data in localStorage, add integrity checks using HMAC and store encryption keys separately
Use `crypto.subtle.digest()` to validate CSS IDs against a whitelist rather than regex escaping
Add CSRF token validation to all state-changing API calls (check server implementation)
Review `.env` / wrangler secrets configuration to ensure no secrets in client-side bundles (not visible in provided files)
